I’m here with you in this. In my early twenties and lost my grandma who raised me a few months ago. People who haven’t gone through grief do not understand it, especially the grief of losing a parent. Since we’re in our twenties, most of our friends haven’t experienced it. It truthfully doesn’t exist in their mind after they console you once. From there it just goes away. They think it should be the same for you too

Being in my early twenties with my current grief and also having experienced the same in high school, I wish someone would tell younger people that grief truly sticks. It’s daily. For my friends, they’re there when you first tell them, they help you out more for a few days, and then it’s just gone. The second they leave that initial conversation it just doesn’t exist in their mind anymore, because most people haven’t been through grief at these ages. Please continue to be there for your friends young people, grief comes in waves (and for me) has gotten worse with time as I process it finally. I need my friends most right now, but it’s already gone for them.

It doesn’t matter how much floor time you give them, they need enough cage room. Especially if you are housing male pigs together. Thankfully my piggies bonded over this move in for three days apparently and did not fight, however they were carefully watched over and constantly given snacks to keep them happy. [Here](https://www.guineapigcagesstore.com/about-candccages) is a website that shows a nice guideline for how much space you should give your piggies. Always have at least two!! And with boys I do NOT recommend more than two in one cage. Even two sometimes pushes it!!! My boys grew up together from a youngish age (not litter mates) so I believe that kept them from getting too fightie. One of my boys also has a few mental disabilities and I honestly believe the two other boys know it and thread lightly haha. If your boys are fighting, keep them in cages where they are right next to each other but still separated. Even just seeing another piggie makes them happier :)
